claim_being_audited: Whether the current release can be certified as policy-compliant on the present record, based on aggregate readiness and rehearsal results, with the logistics customs triage weakness handled through current release documentation rather than prior approval.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is either disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.
Use suspicious when the record points toward the actor's rationale but a required policy predicate or support link is still missing.
Do not treat prior approval or informal monitoring comments as substitutes for current documentation or reviewed acceptance.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release documentation or model-card text showing the logistics customs triage limitation is explicitly disclosed in the launch materials.
Provide any approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering this segment weakness before launch.
Provide the materiality determination, if any, showing why this subgroup regression would not require disclosure under the stated policy.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses or show approved mitigation before certification.
Admissible evidence shows a current subgroup regression in logistics customs triage 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold.
Admissible evidence shows only an informal post-launch monitoring comment; it does not show reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval is explicitly stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and eval batch, so it cannot carry the certification on its own.
Aggregate readiness and a clean rehearsal support launch readiness generally, but they do not satisfy the separate disclosure-or-approved-mitigation predicate for the current segment weakness.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify on the current record is not fully supported because no admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation already includes the required disclosure.
The packet implies the certification predicate can be satisfied through documentation, but the actual current documentation or approved risk acceptance is not in evidence.
